A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Logistic Bandits by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 8 and Appendix A report original synthetic and classification-to-bandit experiments, including cumulative regret and effective-dimension sensitivity results.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A retain original experiments. Appendix J adds synthetic, classification, and Open Bandit Dataset replay results.

M1.justification: Appendix I introduces NeuralLog-TS-1 and NeuralLog-TS-2, which sample Gaussian latent rewards and select the largest draw. These add distinct exploration procedures to the retained NeuralLog-UCB algorithms.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds three synthetic reward functions, magic, banknote and phoneme classification datasets, and fashion e-commerce data from the Open Bandit Dataset. Logged-feedback evaluation substantially extends the original synthetic and classification coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 4–5 and Table 2 compare the two new Thompson sampling variants alongside the original five methods. The external baseline set remains NCBF-UCB, Logistic-UCB-1 and ada-OFU-ECOLog; Verma's citation update does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: The new OBD protocol uses the random/all split, five candidate actions, matching-action replay, 2,000 accepted events, and cumulative reward/CTR instead of regret. Appendix A also changes MNIST resizing from 14×14 to 7×7 while retaining the stated 196 features, leaving actual preprocessing unresolved; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 6 extends effective-dimension sensitivity analysis to the added synthetic functions. Figures 7–9 add OBD robustness studies varying network width, kappa and S, examining performance with small networks and potentially misspecified theoretical parameters.

E5.justification: The original experiments retain ten repetitions and 96% confidence intervals. Appendix J.1 specifies five repeated runs for the new replay experiment, adding run-count information without establishing any reduction in repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 retain identical plots, while Figures 4–9 and Table 2 add results. At OBD m=20, kappa=50 and S=1, CTR is 0.0050 for TS-1, 0.0041 for TS-2 and 0.0025 for UCB-2. These are new-setting results. Figure 6(i), however, reuses Figure 3(i)'s plot under a different reward-function label.

T1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds an explicit argument for Lemma 5.1, whose v1 counterpart, Lemma 7.1, had an unresolved proof reference. Appendix I adds a Thompson sampling regret derivation and discusses the TS-2 analysis obstacle; Appendix K derives computational costs. The original UCB regret bounds remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: the variance- and data-adaptive concentration inequality, two UCB algorithms and their regret dependences. The Thompson sampling additions remain appendix extensions.

C2.justification: Appendix K newly identifies computational dependence on network parameter count despite improved regret dependence. Remark I.2 explains why TS-2 does not inherit UCB-2's favorable kappa guarantee. Appendix J.1 explicitly qualifies applicability to logged data where theoretical assumptions and parameter values may be misspecified.

D1.justification: Appendix J adds dataset preprocessing and OBD implementation details, including one-hot encoding, 16/8-dimensional user/item SVD embeddings, affinity and interaction features, and accepted-event training updates. These extend the existing implementation documentation; the hardware disclosure is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Saito et al. (2020), Zenati et al. (2022), and Lee and Oh (2024), and expands computational-efficiency positioning. Several other references, including Verma's work, receive publication updates rather than representing newly cited research.

P1.justification: Much original prose is retained. v2 merges the first algorithm's presentation with its results, places both algorithms before joint regret analyses, expands the martingale explanation, and updates headings, affiliations and cross-references.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, reformats Table 1 and the pseudocode, and adds Figures 4–9 and Table 2. Existing Figures 1–3 retain their plots while being repositioned and resized.

improvement.justification: Broader experiments, implementation details and explicit limitations are useful gains. However, the new Appendix F.1 proof does not clearly resolve v1's proof gap: term 7 drops Z_t's regularizer and applies Lemma C.5 across different parameter iterates without controlling their difference. The contradictory MNIST dimensions and reuse of Figure 3(i) as Figure 6(i) under another reward function introduce further reliability problems. These benefits and unresolved problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
